source.title: Iterate Averaging Helps: An Alternative Perspective in Deep Learning
source.authors: Diego Granziol; Nicholas P. Baskerville; Xing-Chen Wan; Samuel Albanie; Stephen J. Roberts

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper, though its header has placeholder publication details (“Published TBD” and “Editor: TBD”).
record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out performance of adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers, including after iterate averaging, using test accuracy or perplexity rather than the original studies’ exact setups.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports theoretical analyses of iterate averaging and sharpness metrics. It does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, large-batch effects, dropout, or memorized-example removal. Values used only as prior-work comparisons are not included.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers on held-out image accuracy and language-model perplexity, and tests whether averaging and changes to adaptivity remove the V4 performance gap. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors argue that iterate averaging, adequate regularization and appropriate adaptivity can make adaptive methods competitive with or better than SGD, and report preliminary evidence of reduced tuning sensitivity and continued late-training improvement. Qualify this conclusion: ordinary Gadam remains below SGD on ImageNet-32, its strongest full-ImageNet results sacrifice convergence speed, and PTB uses L2 regularization rather than decoupled weight decay. The Hessian-sharpness analysis is an ancillary finding.
record.recipe_differences: Tests optimizer comparisons and the effect of adding iterate averaging with weight decay; it does not reproduce the original limited-tuning comparisons as specified in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with optimizer and whether iterate averaging is used; the paper also reports dependence on learning rate, weight decay, averaging frequency, and averaging start point.

fits_no_version.finding: Unscaled Hessian spectral norm, Frobenius norm and trace show no clear correspondence with held-out performance across the Appendix E.1 optimizer settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Common unscaled Hessian sharpness measures need not rank generalization across optimizer recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: SWA changes held-out accuracy relative to plain SGD in the no-batch-normalization experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Averaging non-adaptive SGD iterates can improve held-out performance depending on learning rate.

record.problems: Optimizer tuning was uneven: authors state adaptive methods were not tuned as much and AdamW results may not be optimal. Several ImageNet table results provide no uncertainty estimates. Table 13 sharpness comparisons were explicitly not rigorously tuned.
record.rows_left_out: Optimizer and averaging-frequency experiments in Sections 9–10, additional CIFAR-10 results in Appendix D.1, and Lookahead comparisons in Appendix B are not extracted because the selected rows cover the main cross-optimizer comparisons for V4; the paper also reports many validation metrics and prior-work comparisons not retained here.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

A controlled learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning protocol across all comparisons; comprehensive equal-budget broader tuning; switching from Adam to SGD. Equal or better adaptive training performance is not established for every reported held-out comparison.
Empirical batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions, small-data failures, excessive dropout and removal together with weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized training examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

missing.what: ResNet-18 ImageNet comparison: SGD 69.72%, AdamW 69.92%, Gadam 70.11%. This is an explicitly excluded architecture without the adaptive disadvantage.
missing.locator: Section 7, paragraph following the ImageNet tuning discussion

missing.what: Scheduled Adam test perplexity 61.51 and NT-ASGD 64.73, alongside the manually triggered ASGD comparator 61.98. Scheduling changes the optimizer ranking.
Padam(W) comparisons: CIFAR-100 ResNeXt-29 82.37±0.35, VGG-16 74.56±0.19 and PRN-110 77.30±0.11; ImageNet-32 top-1 59.65±0.17. These reveal optimizer-dependent exceptions.

Matched averaged-SGD comparators: SWA accuracies 82.95±0.28 on ResNeXt-29, 62.32±0.13 on ImageNet-32, 74.57±0.27 on VGG-16 and 77.92±0.36 on PRN-110; ImageNet ResNet-50/101 76.32/78.08. Gadam does not uniformly outperform SGD when both are averaged.
Ranger ImageNet accuracies 75.64 on ResNet-50 and 75.62 on ResNet-101 versus SGD 75.63 and 77.37: approximately tied on one architecture and worse on the other.
ResNet-50 Gadam with the small-scale recipe reaches 75.52%, slightly below SGD's 75.63%; increasing its learning rate to 0.003 reaches 76.53% while sacrificing convergence speed.
Training accuracies for the Table 13 contrasts: AdamW 99.93% versus SGD 99.75%, despite worse test accuracy; Gadam at terminal rate 3E−5 reaches 99.97% training accuracy but remains worse on test.

record.verdict_notes: States describe the adaptive disadvantage in V4: worse adaptive performance is observed; better adaptive performance is reversed. Recovery interventions receive limits_scope because V4 already allows recipe-dependent recovery. No blanket challenge is warranted for an 'often' claim. The tuning protocol also searches weight decay and often fixes Adam's learning rate, so it is not an exact replication of the limited-tuning clause. Results explicitly declared in rows_left_out were not treated as extraction omissions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Broader tuning across the benchmarks and optimizer settings described in the version; switching from Adam to SGD as a tested intervention.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples.
